title: Evals for High-Stakes AI Agents — Doneyli De Jesus & Annabell Schäfer, Langfuse
talk_summary: Langfuse engineers describe an AI engineering loop (trace → monitor → dataset → experiment → eval) for making non-deterministic agents reliable, with a banking-assistant demo. The concrete mechanisms are golden datasets built from production traces plus domain-expert annotation, blended LLM-judge and deterministic code evaluators, and CI gates that run experiments on prompt/config changes.

takeaways.technique: Golden dataset from production traces + expert annotation
takeaways.what_they_do: Curate a representative sample of production traces, have a domain expert label them in an annotation queue with a few simple scores plus free-text comments, then use an LLM to cluster the comments into failure-mode categories that become eval dimensions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you're not asking the the the theme to invent categories. You're just telling them, give me your unfiltered raw commentary on these traces and then you're going to use an LLM to then figure out the categories

takeaways.technique: Blend LLM-judge with deterministic code evaluators
takeaways.what_they_do: For each quality dimension pick either an LLM-as-judge evaluator or a deterministic code evaluator (regex/exact match), deliberately mixing both so scores aren't 100% dependent on a stochastic judge.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the more that you can have a mix um a balance mix that is depending on the type of categories that you identify between LLM as a judge evaluators and deterministic evaluators the better

takeaways.what_they_do: Promoting a prompt version or agent config triggers a CI job that runs the experiment against the golden dataset and returns pass/fail per evaluator with minimum thresholds, producing an evidence trail before merge.
takeaways.evidence_quote: anytime a change hits on your agent, then a CI job is going to kick off to run the experiment against the data set. It's going to evaluate your agent with a new configuration and it's going to give you a pass fail gate

takeaways.what_they_do: Run experiments that change exactly one thing (prompt, model, tool description, context) against the same dataset so results are interpretable, rather than changing several at once.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you want to check if the same model performs better with a different prompt, you ideally only change the prompt and not five other things

takeaways.technique: Calibrate LLM judge against human labels, bias to false positives
takeaways.what_they_do: Label a representative sample by hand, tune the LLM judge to agree with those labels, and initially tune toward over-catching (more false positives) then relax over time.
takeaways.evidence_quote: ideally you just start with having a a few too many false positives so you catch a little more than necessary but don't miss anything and then you just tune it down over time

takeaways.what_they_do: Aggregate scores into dashboards ranked by failure-mode occurrence over time, then filter traces by a specific failure mode to shrink thousands of traces to dozens for targeted investigation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: instead of me having to go through thousands or hundreds of thousands of traces trying to figure out which one is the activity from the agent that is causing the most errors
